A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same d3LLM work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, GPU throughput measurements, component ablations, curriculum sensitivity studies, and appendix comparisons for coder models and EAGLE-3.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds AUP sensitivity analyses, SDTT comparisons, and SGLang throughput experiments.

M1.justification: Pseudo-trajectory distillation, curriculum schedules, losses, multi-block decoding, KV-cache refresh, and early stopping remain unchanged. The one-token teacher steps and generation beyond EOS are newly documented details. SGLang implements the existing decoding algorithm in another backend without a stated algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The training datasets and mathematical reasoning and coding coverage are retained, including long-context GSM8K and the HumanEval+/MBPP+ coder evaluations. New experiments use existing GSM8K coverage. ParallelBench is newly cited but not evaluated; Figure 9's corrected caption does not change its four existing tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds evaluated SDTT-LLaDA baselines using reverse and forward KL losses. Table 15 adds Qwen3-8B to the new SGLang comparison alongside Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct. Existing main benchmark, coder, and EAGLE-3 comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation protocols with weighting-function, alpha, and accuracy-cutoff sweeps; matched SDTT training controls and learning-rate selection; and SGLang evaluation with TP=1 on B200, H100, and A100. Table 15 tests d3LLM at batch sizes 1 and 4 while AR rows use batch size 1. These are added protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's component ablations and curriculum studies remain. v3 adds substantial validation of the proposed AUP metric: exponential, power, and linear weighting functions in Table 8, alpha sensitivity for both model families in Tables 10–11, and accuracy-cutoff sensitivity in Table 13. These directly test whether comparative rankings depend on previously untested metric choices.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain standard deviations over three runs, and the existing ablation uncertainty reporting is unchanged. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are introduced. The added appendix results use point estimates, a practice already present in v1.

E6.justification: New results establish stable rankings across the tested AUP variants, compare SDTT AUP scores of 309.71/310.33 with d3LLM's 637.65, and report SGLang throughput reaching 1310.2 TPS on B200 at batch size 4. Existing entries are also corrected: D2F's GSM8K AUP changes from 209.7 to 213.8, Fast-dLLM-v2's from 156.0 to 176.1, and coder MBPP AUP from 186.4 to 186.2. The new backend results are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 mathematically defines power and linear alternatives to AUP's exponential weighting and generalizes its cutoff to ymin = y1 - delta_y for sensitivity analysis. The original AUP aggregation and pseudo-trajectory construction equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and principal claims: balancing accuracy and parallelism through distillation and decoding, introducing AUP, leading on nine of ten comparisons, and achieving up to approximately 10× diffusion-model and 5× AR speedups. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 explains why AUP is not directly optimized, acknowledges that global trajectory sampling does not guarantee the exact local mask ratio, and argues for preserving the teacher's global ordering. It adds interpretations of SDTT and SGLang results. Appendix C largely restates the foundation-model applicability discussion already present in v1.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A.11 clarify one-token teacher decoding, continuation beyond EOS, and global trajectory indexing. New experiments document SDTT tuning and SGLang integration, thresholds, hardware, batch sizes, and tensor parallelism. Most training details were already supplied in v1 and are relocated; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion expands to MDLM, RADD, SDTT, Duo, and ParallelBench, adding context on earlier diffusion training, distillation, and parallel-decoding trade-offs. Further citations cover serving and potential extensions. The original diffusion-versus-speculative-decoding positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the AUP explanation and method motivation, moves training details and the hardware-independence remark into the appendix, and expands appendix organization. It also updates the title and conference information and adds acknowledgements, an impact statement, and a limitations section. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Six new tables substantially expand the evidence displays: weighting-function comparisons, two alpha-sensitivity tables, SDTT results, cutoff sensitivity, and a GPU/batch-size throughput matrix. Existing figures and tables are retained with layout adjustments and renumbering; Figure 9's inaccurate task caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: The AUP sensitivity tests and controlled SDTT comparison add useful validation missing from v1, while SGLang experiments and trajectory clarification strengthen practical evidence and reproducibility. Several numerical inconsistencies are corrected. The gains remain bounded: new validation concentrates on GSM8K, and reporting inconsistencies persist, including default D2F AUP of 213.8 in Tables 1/10 versus 209.7 in Table 13. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
